spreadsheet.title: Bring the spreadsheet with you
spreadsheet.heroLede: The sheet you keep is the file: one row per diver, saved as CSV. What follows is the column list it reads, then the four jobs it takes on that a list never did.
spreadsheet.wedgeIntro1: A spreadsheet holds the names and the numbers and checks none of them. The checking, cards, waivers, who is still not ready, is what you do by hand right now.
spreadsheet.wedgeIntro2: The four jobs it takes on:

cardsChecked.title: Every certification checked before the boat leaves
cardsChecked.body: Each diver’s certification is read against what the trip and the site require. Anyone who can’t board yet is listed, with the reason.

blockersOnePlace.title: Who can’t board yet, in one list
blockersOnePlace.body: Needs you, on Today, lists who still can’t board and why: a missing waiver, or a certification nobody has verified yet.

diversBookThemselves.title: Divers book and sign themselves
diversBookThemselves.body: A diver picks a seat and signs the waiver from a link, with no account and no app. An unsigned one is on Today the night before, with the name.

manifestHeadCount.title: A manifest that calls the roll by name
manifestHeadCount.body: The crew marks each diver and crew member aboard by name, dive by dive, on a phone, from a copy saved to it before the boat leaves, so the roll call keeps working with no signal at the ramp.

spreadsheet.columnsIntro: One row per diver, saved as CSV. Your headings don’t have to match these; the common names are recognized, and the preview names any it isn’t sure of.

name.detail: First and last in two columns, or one full-name column. The only thing a row needs.

email.detail: How DiveDay reaches a diver and recognizes a returning one, so a second import updates instead of duplicating. A row without one still comes in.

phone.detail: Mobile or landline, however you’ve written it.

dateOfBirth.detail: A real date of birth carries over when your file has one.

emergencyContact.detail: A name and a phone number, when you have them, land on the diver’s record.

diveInsurance.detail: A DAN number or a provider name comes across as written. Never a gate; it is what the crew wants on hand in an incident.

certification.detail: Agency, level, and certification number. The certification number is what lets a record come across at all.

specialty.detail: Deep, wreck, night, or drysuit. One cell can name several (“Deep, Wreck”) and each becomes its own certification under the diver’s agency number.

nitrox.detail: A yes/no column, plus the nitrox certification number if you keep one. The number is what brings it across.

rentalSizes.detail: BCD, wetsuit, boot, and fin. Whatever sizes you track become a fit profile.

pastVisits.detail: A date, trip name, and price per row becomes that diver’s history here, so a regular arrives as a regular. Repeat their email on each row to match the right person.

waivers.detail: A signed waiver claim and safe document links can come across; individual medical answers do not.

paymentHistory.detail: Payment, refund, and receipt rows can be kept as unverified history, never as live card data.

notes.detail: Staff and diver notes become private notes on the diver’s profile.

gearHistory.detail: A separate gear CSV brings in your tagged units and dated service, hydro, inspection, O2-clean, and condition records.

spreadsheet.parallelRunNote: Keep the sheet going as long as you like. A re-import matches divers by email and updates them instead of duplicating, so the day you stop keeping it is yours to pick.
spreadsheet.closingTitle: The demo is the shop your sheet would land in
spreadsheet.closingDescription: Open it as the owner, the captain or a diver. No sign-up, and nothing in it is yours to break.
